source.exact_statement: For every r>=1 and widths w_j>=1, let U=product_j OR(X_j), with disjoint private blocks X_j of widths w_j, T=z OR U on one shared coordinate z, and f=2T-1. Put epsilon_j=2^(-w_j), a=product_j(1-epsilon_j), J=a sum_j w_j epsilon_j/(1-epsilon_j). Then physical I(f)=1-a+J. Let Q be the normalized A006 anchored clause-mask union law on supports {z} union X_j, with t_j=epsilon_j/2, empty mass 1-t_j and each nonempty mask mass t_j^2/(1-t_j). The fixed normalized reference R=(delta_{ {z}}+Q)/2 satisfies sum_{A nonempty} hat(f)(A)^2 log2(1/R(A)) <=(29/2) I(f); the standard empty/nonempty wrapper costs at most (33/2) I(f). For all w_j=2 and r>=4, the unaugmented Q instead has nonempty cross-entropy divided by I(f)>3(r-1)/224, although H(f)<6 I(f).
hypotheses: Uniform physical cube; all private X_j are mutually disjoint and disjoint from the one shared coordinate z.
Representation, z and widths are public before the spectral set is sampled; R is fixed for the whole spectral set.
Entropy and logarithmic code costs use base 2. Claims concern logarithmic cost with standard asymptotic arithmetic coding, not an uncharged integral prefix length.
